title: The Farm Shop
strapline: Fresh eggs, muddy carrots, apples in crates and honey in jars — food straight from the farm to the shop to you.
intent: A farm shop connects the food children eat with the farm it grew on, and playing at running one builds real knowledge of where food comes from and the people who grow and sell it.
Weighing, pricing, bagging and selling fresh produce is genuine, purposeful mathematics — counting, weighing, money, and 'how much' and 'how many'.
Serving customers, taking orders and chatting over the counter is real conversation with a real purpose.
Sorting and handling real fruit, vegetables, eggs and produce grows fine-motor control and knowledge of the natural world and the seasons.
Prices, labels, signs and receipts give writing and reading a genuine job.
Vocabulary and community knowledge grow — farm, fresh, weigh, produce, harvest, market, customer, seasonal.
implementation: Stock a farm shop with real or realistic produce — vegetables with the soil still on, eggs, apples in crates, jars of honey and jam — plus scales, a till and bags.
Take the customer role so children weigh, price, bag and sell: 'I'd like a kilo of potatoes, please — how much will that be?'
Model the shopkeeper's talk and the food's story: 'These carrots were pulled from the ground this morning — that's why they're still muddy.'
Bring in maths through the play — weigh produce on the scales, count eggs into boxes, handle coins and prices, compare more and less, heavier and lighter.
Leave price labels, signs, a chalkboard of today's specials and receipt pads so writing and number have a real job.
Link it to real knowledge — what grows in which season, the journey from farm to shop to plate — and connect it to your own growing and cooking.
key_questions: I'd like a kilo of potatoes — how much will that be?
Why are these carrots still muddy?
How many eggs fit in this box?
Which crate is heavier — the apples or the potatoes?
What grows in which season — is this a summer or a winter vegetable?

impact.text: Children connect the food they eat to the farm it grew on and the people who grow and sell it.
Children weigh, price, bag and sell produce — genuine, purposeful mathematics.
Children serve customers and take orders — real conversation with a real purpose.
Children read and write price labels, signs and receipts, giving print a genuine job.
Children sort and handle real produce, growing fine-motor control and seasonal knowledge.

enhancements: Real or realistic produce with the soil still on, plus scales, a till and bags.
A chalkboard of today's specials and receipt pads for real writing.
A link to the setting's own growing — what was picked from the garden goes on sale.
A seasonal produce chart showing what grows when.
Egg boxes and crates for counting and grouping the stock.

playing_exploring: Children run the farm shop in role, handling real produce and stepping confidently into serving and selling.
They explore the fruit, vegetables and scales as they weigh and sort.
active_learning: Children keep the shop going through a busy queue, weighing, pricing and serving customer after customer.
creating_thinking: Children work out weights, prices and totals, and make links from the shop shelves back to the farm and the seasons.
